not_covered: I did not play 40 turns by hand or reach a winning Council vote on screen; AI play quality, battle fairness, prices and balance are other tracks. Tech and unit counts, town development, credit and the transport rules were judged from code and probes, not from play. Original-game numbers were not re-verified against the PDF (not allowed); Firefox and mobile widths not tried.

findings.title: No technology tree: 28 technologies, the purchase screen and research are missing
repro: Open http://localhost:3170/, click Open Capital.
Look at the Technology button in the dialog header (greyed out, tooltip "Coming in a later milestone").
Search the order list: Order.ts has 27 order kinds and none buys a technology.
findings.expected: Rules 09: 28 technologies bought with cash on a technology screen, each unlocking rail terrain, civilians, levels, buildings, units and ships; techs appear by year window.
findings.actual: The game has 5 technology flags in a list shared by both nations (technologyState). Only 2 are the real start techs (High Pressure Steam Engine, Seed Drill); Compound Steam Engine, Iron Railroad Bridge and Dynamite are given free by decision Q8/NR-015. Nothing can be bought, and nothing but rail/depot-on-hills reads the list. Planning note: the game ends in Winter 1824, so a faithful tech tree would show at most 5 of the 26 purchasable techs (windows 1816-1825); the game length must be decided together with the tech tree.

findings.title: Minor nations are constant machines: fixed offers and demand, endless money, price only moves with the two Great Powers
repro: Open Market and compare turn 1 and turn 10: the sellers and "Buyers: 2 units" lines never change.
Read the header text: "buy only clothing, furniture and hardware".
findings.expected: Rules 06 section 4 and gaps A2/C5: price is set by all countries' supply and demand; minors offer and buy more or less depending on last turn's price, year and relations.
findings.actual: Each minor offers 1 unit per resource tile (cap 6) and bids for exactly 2 clothing, 2 furniture, 2 hardware every turn, forever. Minors' own volume moves no price (only Great Power net deals do, tradeSystem.ts:21-27), so prices are a bounded random walk (3% a turn, 50% to 250%) rather than a market. Steel, lumber, fabric, paper, canned food and armaments have no buyer except a rival that happens to bid.

findings.title: No credit, interest or forced sale; the Deal Book is not the original ledger
repro: Open Deal Book after a turn with a purchase.
Compare with rules 06 section 7.5: Sold, Bought, Military Upkeep, Overseas Profits, Interest, net, Credit Limit.
Let treasury fall below the upkeep: newest regiments are disbanded.
findings.expected: Rules 06 section 6: you may end a trade phase in debt up to a credit limit that grows with income; interest above half the limit; beyond it stock is force-sold; spending orders are checked against cash plus credit.
findings.actual: Nation.creditLimit (5000) and Nation.debt (0) are set at start and never read. Orders need cash on hand; unpaid upkeep disbands the newest regiments (decision Q36, "v2 has no credit"). The Deal Book bottom line has Sold, Bought, Military upkeep, Trade net plus a treasury block where all domestic spending (jobs, mills, workers) is one lump "Other (building, workers, gold, gems)". There are no wages in Imp1 and none here (that matches).
